newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain unions meet today, finalise job reform offer.
newsitem.headline: Spain unions meet today, finalise job reform offer.

text.p: Leading Spanish trade unions are to meet today to finalise an offer for the reform of the labour market, a source at union CCOO said on Tuesday.
The proposal should be presented to employers later this week, possibly on Tuesday or Wednesday.
But so far the discusssions are still problematic, with both sides far from agreement.

"Today there's an executive meeting between the two unions (UGT and CCOO). Probably tomorrow they will present this to the employers. They're in the final stages but it seems (the talks) are facing difficulties," the source said.
The meeting tomorrow with bosses was likely to be of a technical nature, but the unions may hold a press conference detailing their offer to them either tomorrow or Wednesday.
A spokeswoman for employers association CEOE said there may be a meeting with unions on Friday, but this has not been finalised.
CEOE has so far declined to comment on the talks' progress.
Speaking in Barcelona on Monday, CCOO's general secretary Antonio Gutierrez said the two sides might need more time before government intervention, "the worst solution," in his view.
The government has given both sides until early March to reach agreement on how to make the labour market more flexible and bring down the unemployment rate, which is Europe's highest.
The unions are expected to announce a proposal to create a special contract to introduce more jobs for youth, and a new apprenticeship contract.
CCOO's Gutierrez denied that the unions were proposing that more criteria could be justified as fair dismissal.
"At no time have we suggested that the causes of fair dismissal should be extended," for example, to include a firm's competitiveness.
But, he explained, "neither should we have to wait for (a firm's) bankruptcy before it can adjust its personnel."
"Competitivity cannot be a cause for (fair) dismissal and if what they want is to justify a sacking, the best possible justification would be that which has union backing."
Gutierrez reiterated union demands for more participation in decisions to dismiss employees, in order to more clearly establish and specify reasons for fair dismissal.
On Sunday, the leader of the other leading union UGT said the talks so far were "closer to disagreement than agreement."
